title: policy-synthesis-for-geo-aware-version-pin-and-gradual-traffic-shifts
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Problem: We need a deterministic, low-latency policy engine that composes region selection, tier routing, explicit model-version pinning, and gradual rollout (canary/A-B) weights while also providing safe fallback to compatible model variants when capacity or compatibility constraints occur. Current ad-hoc ordering leads to surprising behavior for canaries (sessions jump regions or variants mid-rollout) and unclear observability for why a request chose a particular variant.

Goal: Deliver a policy synthesis layer and config schema that: (1) preserves user/session affinity during gradual traffic shifts, (2) evaluates deterministic fallback paths when preferred variants are unavailable, (3) supports per-customer and per-route overrides, and (4) emits clear routing reasons & metrics for SLOs and rollbacks.

Key requirements: deterministic hashing for rollout weights with tenant salt; configurable grace windows to keep in-flight sessions on canary; explicit pin precedence semantics; fast evaluation path (sub-ms) on routing plane; observable route decision traces with reasons and variant chain; policy constraints for region and tier that can short-circuit rollouts when required (e.g., data residency).
implementation_notes: Plan: 1) Introduce a compact policy AST (proto) that composes precedence tiers: explicit_pin -> region_constraint -> tier_constraint -> rollout_weight -> fallback_chain. 2) Use a per-tenant stable-hash (fnv64 + salt) to compute rollout assignments so AB splits are deterministic across nodes. 3) Add session affinity token (sticky_id) support that maps to a sticky table with TTL-based grace windows to honor canary for existing sessions. 4) Fallback chain defined as ordered compatible variant list (e.g., base-16b -> quantized-8bit -> small-llm -> embed-only) with explicit degrade actions (rerank-only, partial-response). 5) Minimal runtime cost: implement evaluator in C++ runtime path and expose a fast path cache for common policy decisions. 6) Provide config migration tooling to translate existing pinning/rollout configs into the new schema.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Deterministic hashing simplifies dev ops but requires careful per-tenant salt management; salt change invalidates assignments.
- Sticky tables add memory and eventual-consistency concerns across distributed routing nodes; mitigated by TTLs and lease windows.
- Adding evaluator code on the hot path increases complexity and the binary surface; reduce risk via staged rollout and feature flag.
- Fallback semantics may degrade quality if we choose too-small variants; require automated quality regression checks tied to rollout metrics.
- Cross-region failover could violate data residency if not constrained by region constraints; policy schema must support hard-region-blocks.
observability_and_slos: Emit the following tags per request: routing_reason (explicit_pin|region|tier|rollout|fallback), chosen_variant, fallback_chain, rollout_bucket, session_affinity=true/false, decision_latency_ms. Aggregate counters: decisions_by_reason, fallback_rate_by_variant, canary_drop_rate, session_stickiness_breaks. Dashboards: Datadog dashboard to show canary 95/99 latency and token-quality regressions, and a heatmap of fallback rates by region. Alert gates: abort rollout if fallback_rate > 2% over 15m or quality regression (BLEU/ROUGE/QA accuracy delta) > configured threshold.
test_plan: Unit tests for AST evaluation, integration tests simulating capacity loss and region failover, canary session stickiness e2e with dogfood traffic, performance benchmarks (p95 decision latency < 1ms at 10k qps). Add chaos tests that kill preferred variants to assert fallback correctness and metric emissions.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated in control plane only (reads, no enforcement) to validate decisions vs current resolver. 2) Internal dogfood + reliability sprint for 2 weeks. 3) Gradual enforcement on non-critical customers (5% customers) with telemetry gates. 4) Full enforcement across hosted after metric gates pass for two consecutive days. Rollback: control-plane toggle + kill switch in routing nodes to revert to legacy resolver.
open_questions: What is the canonical list of compatible variant downgrades for each model family?
Should sticky_id be optional or enforced for all conversational routes?
How do we rotate tenant salts safely without causing mass reassignment?
